If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to compensate for bearish bias.

If sentiment swings from positive to negative within 5 days, shift forecast downward by 1–2% in mid-horizon (8–15 days) to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast in late horizon (16–30 days) to capture momentum continuation.

If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast in late horizon (16–30 days) to avoid overcorrection.

If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33–0.67) and forecast deviates >1.5% from true path, apply a 0.5–1.0% smoothing correction in mid-late horizon (15–30 days) to dampen noise.
